_comment: One general manager's day, recorded as a 1920x1080 desktop video: 07:00 briefing, 09:40 order question, 11:15 feasibility (chat, then the Feasibility page), 14:30 chase-up, 17:00 watch, and a question the data cannot answer. Times are planned seconds; model waits stretch the run and --compress-waits squeezes them back. Captions are burned into a band under the page.

steps.say: 07:00 — before the manager asks anything, the day is already on one screen.
RED: eight orders overdue, assembly 39% below its normal range for six days, three decisions.
Each decision has one button. Nothing here was asked for: the discovery tool found it.
The 07:00 morning briefing, written on a schedule: yesterday’s output, what is at risk, what to decide today.
The full briefing: production, priorities and action items, each with its supporting records. The actions become the day’s to-do list.
09:40 — on the floor. “How is the TrendCart order doing?”

type.text: How is the TrendCart order doing?

steps.say: TrendCart has six orders, so it asks instead of guessing.
Now it knows which order: ORD-005, 500 scarves, at knitting, due 20 April, idle 8 days. Every number opens its source rows.
11:15 — “A customer wants 800 hoodies by the 25th. Can we take it?”

type.text: Can we take 800 hoodies by the 25th?

steps.say: It asks the one thing that changes the answer: ready at the factory, or delivered?
An estimate with its assumptions: the queue’s finish date, the on-time chance, the bottleneck stage. Not a yes.
Can the factory take on more orders? The Feasibility page runs the same tool over the whole queue.
Our own queue finishes 30 April, after the 25th; an eligible outside workshop could make 10 April, its stage coverage still to be checked.
Why: the queued work plus this order is over capacity at assembly, washing and packing before the 25th.
14:30 — “That order hasn’t moved in a week. Chase it up.”

type.text: That order hasn’t moved in a week. Chase it up.

steps.say: It checks the claim first: last activity 24 March, 8 days ago, then drafts to the knitting team. Nothing is sent yet.
Preview first. Sending needs the manager’s confirmation, and it is logged.
Sent, and recorded in the activity log with who, when and what.
17:00 — “Remind me tomorrow if packing is still behind.”

type.text: Remind me tomorrow if packing is still behind.

steps.say: A standing watch: the server checks packing against its normal range tomorrow and only speaks if it is still behind.
Confirmed. The watch runs on the server; nothing leaves the system until it fires.
And when there is no answer in the data, it says so.

type.text: What revenue did the TrendCart orders bring in this quarter?

steps.say: No prices in the data, so no revenue figure. It never invents one.
ThreadPilot: the general manager’s co-pilot, all day, with every number traceable.
